sci: Delphinidae and the river dolphin families
ov: Around 40 species of toothed whale, from the 1.7 m Maui’s dolphin to the orca, the largest at 9.5 m. Most live in the sea, but a few live in rivers in South Asia and South America.

why.et: Dolphin meat is eaten in a few countries, including Japan and Peru.

rg: Oceans worldwide, plus a few large rivers in South Asia and South America.
df: Mostly fish and squid, caught with cone-shaped teeth. The largest dolphins, such as the orca, also hunt seals and other marine mammals.

cf.tip: A porpoise has flat, spade-shaped teeth and usually no pronounced beak. Dolphins have cone-shaped teeth, and most have a beak.

fx: Some dolphins can briefly swim at 29 km/h or leap about 9 m.
